subject: maths
title: Index laws for multiplying and dividing

scenes.heading: Index laws for multiplying and dividing
scenes.say: What is x to the power of twenty, times x to the power of fifteen? Writing out thirty-five x's would take ages. The index laws let you do it in one step.
scenes.caption: What is x²⁰ × x¹⁵? Writing out 35 x's would take ages. The index laws let you do it in one step.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A row of 3 blocks joined to a row of 4 blocks makes 7 blocks
scenes.science: x³ × x⁴ = x⁷: multiplying powers adds the indices
scenes.breaks: Blocks come in whole numbers, but later you will meet negative indices like x⁻², and the laws still work.
scenes.say: Picture x cubed as a row of three blocks, and x to the fourth as a row of four. Join the rows and you have seven blocks: x to the seventh. Taking blocks away is like dividing: seven blocks take away two leaves five.
scenes.caption: Picture x³ as a row of 3 blocks, and x⁴ as a row of 4. Join the rows and you have 7 blocks: x⁷. Taking blocks away is like dividing: 7 blocks take away 2 leaves 5.

scenes.heading: First index law
parts: the base — it stays the same
scenes.say: The first index law: a to the m, times a to the n, equals a to the m plus n. When you multiply powers with the same base, add the indices. The base stays the same, so two cubed times two to the fourth is two to the seventh, not four to the seventh.
scenes.caption: The first index law: aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ. When you multiply powers with the same base, add the indices. The base stays the same, so 2³ × 2⁴ = 2⁷, not 4⁷.

scenes.heading: Second index law
scenes.say: The second index law: a to the m, divided by a to the n, equals a to the m minus n. When you divide powers with the same base, subtract the indices. So a to the seventh divided by a squared is a to the fifth.
scenes.caption: The second index law: aᵐ ÷ aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ. When you divide powers with the same base, subtract the indices. So a⁷ ÷ a² = a⁵.

scenes.heading: With coefficients
scenes.question: Simplify 2a³b × 4a²b⁵.
scenes.say: Simplify two a cubed b, times four a squared b to the fifth. Multiply the numbers: eight. Then each letter. a cubed times a squared is a to the fifth. b on its own is b to the one, so b to the one times b to the fifth is b to the sixth. The answer is eight a to the fifth, b to the sixth.
scenes.caption: Simplify 2a³b × 4a²b⁵. Multiply the numbers: 8. Then each letter. a³ × a² = a⁵. b on its own is b¹, so b¹ × b⁵ = b⁶. The answer is 8a⁵b⁶.

scenes.heading: Dividing
scenes.question: Simplify 12m⁷n³ ÷ 4m²n.
scenes.say: Now divide twelve m to the seventh n cubed by four m squared n. Twelve divided by four is three. m to the seventh divided by m squared is m to the fifth. n cubed divided by n is n squared. The answer is three m to the fifth n squared.
scenes.caption: Now divide 12m⁷n³ by 4m²n. 12 ÷ 4 = 3. m⁷ ÷ m² = m⁵. n³ ÷ n = n². The answer is 3m⁵n².

points: Coefficients: multiply or divide as usual
x on its own is x¹
scenes.say: Quick recap. Multiplying powers with the same base, add the indices. Dividing, subtract them. The base never changes. Multiply or divide the coefficients as normal numbers. And remember, x on its own is x to the power of one. Now try the practice questions!
